name: Formentera
title: Holidays in Formentera
intro: Ibiza's small, quiet neighbour, with white sand, astonishingly clear water and lanes made for cycling. Here's what Formentera is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The white lighthouse of Far de la Mola on Formentera under a blue sky
facts_note: There's no airport, so fly to Ibiza and take the 30-minute ferry from Ibiza Town. The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: June and September are perfect: hot, calm and not too busy, with the sea at its warmest in September. July and August are lovely but crowded with day-trippers from Ibiza, and prices peak. May and October are quieter and cheaper. From November to March much of the island closes.

things.name: Ses Illetes
things.blurb: A long finger of white sand with turquoise water on both sides, often called one of Europe's best beaches.

things.name: Cala Saona
things.blurb: A small sandy cove with red cliffs, best at sunset.

things.name: Far de la Mola
things.blurb: A lonely lighthouse on cliffs at the island's eastern tip.

things.name: Cycling the green routes
things.blurb: Flat, quiet paths through pine woods and salt flats. Hire bikes near the port.

things.name: Platja de Migjorn
things.blurb: Kilometres of quiet beach along the south coast, with a few chiringuitos.

things.name: Espalmador
things.blurb: Boat over to a tiny uninhabited island with clear water and a sandy bay.

faqs.question: How do you get to Formentera?
faqs.answer: Fly to Ibiza, then take a ferry from Ibiza Town. Fast boats take about 30 minutes and run often in summer.

faqs.question: Do you need a car on Formentera?
faqs.answer: No. Bikes, scooters and buses cover most of it, as the island is only about 20 kilometres long.

faqs.question: Is Formentera expensive?
faqs.answer: Yes, hotels and beach restaurants cost more than on most Spanish islands. Self-catering apartments help.

faqs.question: Is Formentera a day trip from Ibiza?
faqs.answer: It's easy as a day trip, but staying lets you enjoy the beaches once the day boats leave.
